qs.q: What is the primary distinguishing physical examination feature that differentiates a solid testicular tumour from a benign hydrocele?
o: Hydroceles cause acute skin ulceration, whereas tumours remain completely subepidermal
Testicular tumours are exquisitely tender, whereas hydroceles are completely painless
Hydroceles are associated with systemic fever, whereas tumours present without inflammation
Testicular tumours fail to transilluminate, whereas hydroceles typically transilluminate
qs.e: Testicular neoplasms present as solid, non-translucent masses, which helps clinically distinguish them from fluid-filled benign hydroceles that readily transilluminate. Both conditions can present as scrotal enlargement without acute skin breakdown.
